chapterTitle: Chapter 2: s-Block Elements (Alkali & Alkaline Earth Metals)
title: Chapter 2: s-Block Elements (Alkali & Alkaline Earth Metals)
subject: chemistry-12

questions.question: When burned in excess oxygen, Lithium, Sodium, and Potassium form which characteristic oxides respectively?

options.D: Normal oxides for all three metals

questions.explanation: Small Li⁺ stabilizes the small O²⁻ oxide ion; larger Na⁺ stabilizes O₂²⁻ peroxide; large K⁺ stabilizes O₂⁻ superoxide.

questions.question: Which alkali metal imparts a persistent golden-yellow color to a non-luminous Bunsen flame?
questions.explanation: Sodium atoms emit strong D-lines at 589 nm giving a brilliant golden-yellow flame.

questions.question: In the Down's Cell for the commercial extraction of metallic sodium, calcium chloride (CaCl₂) is added to NaCl in order to:

options.B: Lower the melting point of NaCl from 801°C to approximately 600°C

questions.explanation: CaCl₂ acts as a flux, lowering the melting point from 801°C to ~600°C to reduce energy costs and prevent sodium vaporization.

questions.question: Which of the following alkaline earth metal carbonates has the highest thermal decomposition temperature?
questions.explanation: Ba²⁺ has the largest radius, causing least polarization of the large CO₃²⁻ anion; hence BaCO₃ has the greatest thermal stability.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of Plaster of Paris?
questions.explanation: Gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) loses 1.5 moles of water at 100°C-120°C to form hemihydrate Plaster of Paris (CaSO₄·½H₂O or 2CaSO₄·H₂O).

questions.question: Beryllium differs from other alkaline earth metals because it:

options.A: Forms predominantly covalent compounds due to high polarizing power (small Be²⁺ size)
options.D: Has the lowest ionization energy in Group IIA

questions.explanation: Tiny Be²⁺ has immense charge density, polarizing anions and conferring high covalent character to its compounds (Fajans' rule).

questions.question: Which alkali metal hydroxide is amphoteric and dissolves in excess sodium hydroxide solution?
questions.explanation: Be(OH)₂ is amphoteric, reacting with excess NaOH to form soluble beryllate ion [Be(OH)₄]²⁻.

questions.question: In the Solvay process for manufacturing sodium carbonate, the raw materials consumed are:
questions.explanation: Brine (NaCl), limestone (CaCO₃ source of CO₂ and CaO), and ammonia (NH₃) are the primary raw materials in Solvay's process.

questions.question: Why is sodium stored under kerosene oil or liquid paraffin in the laboratory?

options.B: It reacts rapidly with atmospheric oxygen and moisture to form oxides and hydroxides

questions.explanation: Sodium is highly electropositive and reacts vigorously with moisture and oxygen; hydrocarbons do not react with sodium.

questions.question: What is the role of magnesium ion (Mg²⁺) in biological systems?

options.A: It is the central coordinating metal ion in chlorophyll molecules
options.B: It is the primary cation of extracellular fluids
options.C: It forms the core of hemoglobin

questions.explanation: Mg²⁺ occupies the center of the porphyrin ring in chlorophyll, essential for photosynthetic light absorption.

questions.question: Which of the following Group IIA sulfates is the most soluble in water?
questions.explanation: Be²⁺ has an exceptionally high hydration enthalpy that outweighs the lattice energy of BeSO₄, making it highly water-soluble.

questions.question: When Lithium nitrate (LiNO₃) is heated strongly, it decomposes into:
questions.explanation: Unlike other alkali metal nitrates that yield nitrites and O₂, LiNO₃ decomposes like Group IIA nitrates into Li₂O, NO₂ (brown fumes), and O₂.

questions.question: Which alkaline earth metal produces an apple-green flame in a flame test?
questions.explanation: Barium salts impart a distinctive apple-green coloration to the flame.

questions.question: In Nelson's Cell (diaphragm cell) for manufacturing caustic soda (NaOH), the diaphragm is made of:
questions.explanation: An asbestos diaphragm separates the anode and cathode compartments, preventing Cl₂ from reacting with NaOH.

questions.question: What gas is evolved at the cathode during the electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride (brine)?
questions.explanation: H⁺ (from water) has a higher reduction potential than Na⁺, so 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻ occurs at the cathode.

questions.question: Milk of Magnesia, an over-the-counter antacid and laxative, is an aqueous suspension of:
questions.explanation: Magnesium hydroxide [Mg(OH)₂] suspension neutralizes excess gastric HCl safely without releasing gas.

questions.question: Why does Lithium uniquely react directly with atmospheric Nitrogen upon heating to form a nitride (Li₃N)?

options.B: Small Li⁺ and N³⁻ ions have exceptionally high lattice energy that stabilizes the ionic lattice

questions.explanation: Li₃N is stable because the very small Li⁺ cation packs efficiently with small N³⁻, generating massive lattice energy.

questions.question: The solubility of alkaline earth metal hydroxides down Group IIA (Be(OH)₂ to Ba(OH)₂):
questions.explanation: Lattice energy decreases more rapidly than hydration enthalpy down Group IIA for hydroxides; hence Ba(OH)₂ is the most soluble and basic.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is known as 'Quicklime'?
questions.explanation: Calcium oxide (CaO) is quicklime; upon adding water, it slakes exothermically to form slaked lime [Ca(OH)₂].

questions.question: What is the primary commercial use of metallic Potassium superoxide (KO₂) in closed-circuit breathing apparatus (submarines and space suits)?

options.A: It absorbs CO₂ and releases O₂ gas simultaneously
options.C: It generates heat to warm the cabin
options.D: It serves as a fuel cell catalyst

questions.explanation: 4 KO₂ + 2 CO₂ → 2 K₂CO₃ + 3 O₂; it scrubs exhaled carbon dioxide while replenishing oxygen.

questions.question: The oxidation state of oxygen in potassium superoxide (KO₂) is:
questions.explanation: K has +1 oxidation state; thus O₂ has -1 charge, giving an average oxidation state of -½ per oxygen atom.

questions.question: Which alkali metal is used in photoelectric cells due to its exceptionally low work function and ionization energy?
questions.explanation: Cesium's valence electron is held very loosely (IE = 376 kJ/mol), emitting electrons upon exposure even to visible light.

questions.question: Dead burnt plaster is formed when gypsum is heated above:
questions.explanation: Above 200°C, all water of crystallization is driven off, forming anhydrous CaSO₄ (dead burnt plaster) which sets extremely slowly.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds gives a crimson red flame in flame photometry?
questions.explanation: Strontium salts impart an intense crimson-red color to the flame.

questions.question: Epsom salt, commonly used in bath soaks and medicine, has the formula:
questions.explanation: Epsom salt is magnesium sulfate heptahydrate (MgSO₄ · 7H₂O).

questions.question: When calcium carbide (CaC₂) reacts with water, the hydrocarbon gas evolved is:
questions.explanation: CaC₂ + 2 H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + C₂H₂ (acetylene gas).

questions.question: The chemical formula of soda ash is:
questions.explanation: Anhydrous sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) is termed soda ash, whereas the decahydrate is washing soda.

questions.question: Which s-block element reacts with liquid ammonia to produce a deep blue conducting solution containing ammoniated electrons?
questions.explanation: Alkali metals dissolve in liquid ammonia: Na + (x+y)NH₃ → [Na(NH₃)_x]⁺ + [e(NH₃)_y]⁻. The ammoniated electron absorbs in the red region, imparting deep blue color.

questions.question: Which alkaline earth metal does not give a flame test color because its valence electrons are too tightly bound to be excited by Bunsen burner heat?
questions.explanation: Due to their small size and high ionization energies, Be and Mg electrons require higher energy than a Bunsen flame can provide; hence they emit no visible flame color.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is formed when metallic sodium reacts with dry ammonia gas at 300°C?
questions.explanation: 2 Na + 2 NH₃ → 2 NaNH₂ (sodamide) + H₂ gas.

questions.question: What happens when CO₂ gas is passed continuously through limewater for an extended period?

options.B: The solution turns clear due to the formation of soluble calcium bicarbonate [Ca(HCO₃)₂]

questions.explanation: Initial milkiness is due to insoluble CaCO₃. Continued CO₂ forms soluble Ca(HCO₃)₂: CaCO₃ + CO₂ + H₂O → Ca(HCO₃)₂.

questions.question: The cement industry uses Gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) in amounts of 2% to 5% primarily to:

options.B: Retard the initial setting time of cement

questions.explanation: Gypsum reacts with tricalcium aluminate (C₃A) to form insoluble ettringite crystals, preventing rapid flash setting and retarding the setting time.

questions.question: Which of the following alkali metal halides has the lowest solubility in water due to high lattice energy?
questions.explanation: Both Li⁺ and F⁻ are extremely small, resulting in exceptionally high lattice energy that exceeds hydration energy, making LiF poorly soluble.

questions.question: What is the biological importance of sodium-potassium pumps (Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase) in animal cell membranes?

options.A: Maintains resting membrane potential by pumping 3 Na⁺ ions out and 2 K⁺ ions in per ATP hydrolyzed

questions.explanation: The Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase hydrolyzes ATP to export 3 Na⁺ and import 2 K⁺, maintaining electrical polarization essential for nerve impulses.

questions.question: Which of the following metals burns with an intensely bright white flame and is widely used in flash photography and fireworks?
questions.explanation: Magnesium ribbon burns vigorously in air: 2 Mg + O₂ → 2 MgO with intense emission of white light across UV and visible wavelengths.
